quarterly_data.signal: L3Harris 10-K (fiscal 2025): revenue $21,865 million, up 3%; operating income $2,110 million; diluted EPS $8.53; operating cash flow $3,106 million. Contractual backlog $38.7 billion, up 13% ($26.9 billion funded), with approximately 45% expected to be recognized by the end of fiscal 2026 and approximately 70% by the end of fiscal 2027. Segments: Communication Systems $5,673 million (operating margin 25.2%, backlog $6,935 million); Integrated Mission Systems $6,630 million (12.2%, backlog $12,215 million); Space & Airborne Systems $6,946 million (12.3%, backlog $11,384 million); Aerojet Rocketdyne $2,845 million, up 10% on missile and munitions production volume (9.5%, backlog $8,171 million). International revenue was $4.8 billion (22% of revenue) and 75% of revenue came from fixed-price contracts; company-funded R&D was $536 million; fiscal 2026 capital expenditures are expected to be approximately $600 million. Purchase obligations of approximately $10.2 billion (about 60% due within 12 months) mainly consist of open purchase orders to suppliers, subcontractors and other outsourcing partners under U.S. Government contracts and managed service agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $21,865 million (+3%); backlog $38.7 billion (+13%); 2026 capex approximately $600 million; purchase obligations approximately $10.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: L3Harris 10-K: in Q4 2025 L3Harris agreed with AE Industrial Partners to form a new space technology company from its Space Propulsion and Power Systems business (Aerojet Rocketdyne segment) and its Space Avionics & Communications business (IMS segment), excluding the RS-25 rocket engine business; AE Industrial will acquire an approximately 60% controlling interest and L3Harris will retain a 40% noncontrolling interest, with closing expected in the second half of 2026. L3Harris divested its commercial aviation (CAS) business on March 28, 2025, and from fiscal 2026 reports three segments: Space & Mission Systems, Communication & Spectrum Dominance and Missile Solutions. It relies on a limited number of certified microelectronics component suppliers and on some single-source suppliers, and some materials were previously sourced from areas now under sanctions, such as specialty metals from Russia and certain equipment from China.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 60% to AE Industrial; 40% retained; close expected second half of 2026
